lesson_title: The Balloon That Stole Your Electrons
hook_text: Rub a balloon on your hair and it sticks to the wall. Your hair stands up. Something tiny just changed owners.
clip_script: Rub a balloon on your hair on a dry winter morning and pull it away. Your hair rises after it. Press it on the wall and it stays. What happened? Everything is made of atoms, with positive protons in the middle and negative electrons around them, normally perfectly balanced. Rubbing is a tug of war for electrons, and rubber beats hair. Billions of electrons jumped from your hair onto the balloon. The balloon is now negative. Your hair, missing exactly as many electrons, is positive. Nothing was created. It was just moved. The protons never budge; they are locked in the nucleus. That is why positive always means lost electrons. Try it on a humid day in Durban and it barely works, because damp air lets the charge leak away. And a metal spoon? Its electrons flow straight out through your hand.
visual_style: A whiteboard balloon and a head of hair, then a zoom into atoms with electrons hopping across, then plus signs on the hair and minus signs on the balloon.
pacing: A quick visual trick, then a clear step-by-step reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and predict which material goes negative.
